name: Com-Pac 16
notes: All points are pixels in the 800x895 drawing, read by hand off gridded enlargements and snapped to dark pixels where a column or row scan found the line. Bow is to the right in both views.

The drawing superimposes an accommodation plan (top) on a sail-plan profile (bottom), on one shared x scale: the bow sits at x 705 in the plan and 706 in the profile. At the stern the plan's curved transom bulges to x 116 on the centreline, 7 px aft of the profile's transom; the plan is used as drawn, from the profile transom forward.

Profile hull, transom top to stem head, spans x 123 to 706 = 583 px for an LOA of 16.0 ft, 36.44 px/ft. LWL reads 14.4 ft (spec 14.0), draft 1.72 ft (spec 1.5), beam 6.48 ft off the plan's outer outline (spec 6.0), masthead 21.5 ft above the drawn waterline (spec 21.0).

The drawn draft and beam run 15% and 8% over the spec while mast height agrees within 3%, so the scale is not the cause: the drawing shows a deeper keel and a wider deck than the published figures. The spec page notes later boats were offered with a stainless centreboard; the drawing shows the fixed shoal keel only.
The waterline is the thin line at y 806 drawn clear of both ends; the dark band at y 802-804 directly above it is the boot-top.
Sheer is the top of the three-line rubrail band (bottom line heavy). The cockpit coaming above it aft (y 727) and the forward toerail are not part of the hull outline.

Not traced: the transom-hung rudder, which hangs aft of the transom to x 86 and down to y 879, below the keel; it cannot sit in the hull outline without moving the LOA calibration. Also omitted: shrouds, jib, the tiller, and a hatched strut from the transom top to the boom end (a boom crutch, by its look).

The plan's half-breadths are its outermost line (hull at the rubrail), averaged across both sides about y 439.5; the two sides agree within 3 px. Nothing in the plan is inferred, so inferredFromX sits at the stem head.
